card.title: Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents
card.task: Generating and executing executable Python code as actions for LLM agents to improve their performance in complex real-world tasks.
card.method: CodeAct integrates LLMs with a Python interpreter to generate and execute executable Python code as actions. This approach overcomes limitations of text and JSON-based actions by allowing dynamic adjustment and composition of actions based on new observations and feedback.
benchmarks: A newly curated benchmark consisting of 82 human-curated tasks
baselines: Conventional LLMs generating text or JSON-based actions
LLMs generating code with pre-specified control primitives and hand-engineered prompts
claims: CodeAct outperforms existing methods on a variety of LLMs with up to 20% higher success rate.
CodeAct achieves comparable or better performance than the baselines for most LLMs.
CodeAct's performance gains are particularly significant on complex tasks, often requiring multiple tool calls in multi-turn interactions.
card.runs_or_seeds: Details for reproducibility are not provided, as they are internal and not shared.

quotes.text: This setting overlooks the potential of environmental observation (e.g., code execution results) that might benefit future action and overall decision (e.g., dynamically adjusting subsequent code after observing intermediate code execution results, fixing erroneous code after seeing an error message).
That is, the generated code is a static sequence of actions that cannot be dynamically re-adjusted on the fly by incorporating new observations.
Such a single-turn setting makes it challenging to scale to more challenging problems since even expert human programmers usually cannot write functionally correct code in 14

critiques.weakness: The paper claims CodeAct benefits from multi-turn interactions and existing software packages to perform complex tasks, but the benchmark M3ToolEval is curated for complex tasks requiring the composition of multiple tools. This suggests CodeAct might not necessarily generalize well to different action formats or tasks outside its curated benchmark.

quotes.text: It contains 82 human-curated instances, spanning tasks including web browsing, finance, travel itinerary planning, science, and information processing.

We also evaluate out-of-domain agent tasks using text actions from MiniWob++ (computer tasks, (Kim et al., 2023)) and ScienceWorld (text-based simulator for elementary science curriculum, (Wang et al., 2022a)) to test whether CodeActAgent can generalize to different action formats.

Finally, we include a suite of general LLM evaluation tasks to assess general capability: MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2020) for knowledge-based QA, HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021) for single-turn codegeneration, GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) for single-turn tool-free math reasoning, and MTBench (Zheng et al., 2023) for instruction-following.
